instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Psa 119:59 'think' is to reflect: the psalmist considers his ways and turns his feet to the testimonies; the reflection leads to action. Verses: Psa 119:59.
observations.grounds: When I think on my ways

observations.text: In Dan 7:25 'think' is the Aramaic verb of intending: the one who speaks against the Most High means to change the times and the law. Verses: Dan 7:25.
observations.grounds: shall think to change the times

observations.text: In these four verses 'think' renders the Hebrew word for eye in the idiom 'in the eyes of': what seems right or best to someone. It is how a person sees or judges a matter. Verses: Num 36:6, 2Sa 10:3, 1Ch 19:3, Jer 40:5.
observations.grounds: whom they think best

observations.text: In 2Sa 18:27 'I think' is the watchman's judgment from what he sees: the running of the first is like that of Ahimaaz. It is an impression from sight. Verses: 2Sa 18:27.
observations.grounds: I think the running of the first

observations.text: In these seven verses 'thoughts' are the reasonings of the mind, which come out of the heart, are known or perceived by Jesus, are revealed from many hearts, are futile for the wise, and become evil in the judge. They are inner reasonings with the heart as their place and Jesus as their knower. Verses: Mat 15:19, Mar 7:21, Luk 2:35, Luk 5:22, Luk 6:8, 1Cor 3:20, Jam 2:4.
observations.grounds: out of the heart come evil thoughts

observations.text: In Luk 11:17 'thoughts' is the inner thinking of the hearers that Jesus knows before he answers. Verses: Luk 11:17.
observations.grounds: knowing their thoughts

observations.text: In Luk 1:51 'thoughts' is the mind or understanding of the proud, scattered by the Lord's arm. Verses: Luk 1:51.
observations.grounds: scattered the proud in the thoughts

observations.text: In Mat 9:4, Mat 12:25 and Heb 4:12 'thoughts' is inner reflection that Jesus knows and that the word of God discerns; the two Matthew verses have Jesus answer them, and Hebrews names them with the intentions of the heart. Verses: Mat 9:4, Mat 12:25, Heb 4:12.
observations.grounds: Knowing their thoughts

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:3 'thoughts' are the mind's products or schemes, which Paul fears will be led astray from devotion to Christ as Eve was. Verses: 2Cor 11:3.
observations.grounds: your thoughts will be led astray

observations.text: In 1Cor 2:11 this code is the Greek article in 'the things of a person', which the English renders as a person's thoughts; the verse says only the person's spirit knows them, as only God's Spirit knows God's. Verses: 1Cor 2:11.
observations.grounds: who knows a person

observations.text: In Eze 38:10 'thoughts' is the Hebrew word for words or matters that come up, here the matters that rise in the mind of Gog before he devises a scheme: something arises, then the person works on it. Verses: Eze 38:10.
observations.grounds: thoughts will come into your mind

observations.text: In Lam 3:62 'thoughts' is the murmuring of the assailants, the Hebrew word for what is muttered or devised, set with their lips against the speaker all day. Verses: Lam 3:62.
observations.grounds: The lips and thoughts of my assailants

observations.text: In Ecc 10:20 'thoughts' is the mind or knowledge within, where a person might curse the king; the verse warns that even there it may be carried. Verses: Ecc 10:20.
observations.grounds: Even in your thoughts

observations.text: In Psa 10:4 'thoughts' are the wicked man's schemes or devices, summed up as that there is no God. Verses: Psa 10:4.
observations.grounds: all his thoughts are

observations.text: In these verses 'thoughts' are the purposes and devisings of people: the intention of the heart in Gen 6:5, purposes kept in the heart in 1Ch 29:18, schemes against others, the just thoughts of the righteous and the foul ones of the wicked, the thoughts to be forsaken, thoughts of iniquity, the thoughts God knows and wicked thoughts that lodge within. Verses: Gen 6:5, 1Ch 29:18, Job 21:27, Psa 56:5, Psa 94:11, Pro 12:5, Pro 15:26, Isa 55:7, Isa 59:7, Isa 66:18, Jer 4:14.
observations.grounds: intention of the thoughts of his heart

observations.text: In Psa 40:5, Psa 92:5 and Mic 4:12 'thoughts' are the Lord's: his thoughts toward his people, very deep, and a plan that the nations do not know. Verses: Psa 40:5, Psa 92:5, Mic 4:12.
observations.grounds: Your thoughts are very deep

observations.text: In Isa 55:8 and Isa 55:9 the same word sets God's thoughts against man's: his are not ours and are as high above ours as heaven is above the earth. Verses: Isa 55:8, Isa 55:9.
observations.grounds: my thoughts are not your thoughts

observations.text: In Job 20:2 'thoughts' are the disquieting thoughts that press on Zophar and answer him from within, because of his haste. Verses: Job 20:2.
observations.grounds: my thoughts answer me

observations.text: In Psa 139:2 and Psa 139:17 'thoughts' are what the mind holds: the psalmist's thought is known to God from afar, and God's thoughts are precious and vast to him. Verses: Psa 139:2, Psa 139:17.
observations.grounds: you discern my thoughts from afar

observations.text: In these Aramaic verses 'thoughts' are the thoughts that rise in the mind: in Dan 2:29 thoughts come in bed about what will be, and in the other verses the king's and Daniel's thoughts alarm them. The same thoughts carry revelation in one place and fear in the others. Verses: Dan 2:29, Dan 2:30, Dan 4:19, Dan 5:6, Dan 5:10, Dan 7:28.
observations.grounds: his thoughts alarmed him

observations.text: In Psa 139:23 'thoughts' are the anxious thoughts that the psalmist asks God to search and know, with the heart named beside them. Verses: Psa 139:23.
observations.grounds: Try me and know my thoughts

observations.text: In Luk 12:17 'thought' is reasoning within oneself: the rich man deliberates in himself what to do about his crops. Verses: Luk 12:17.
observations.grounds: he thought to himself

observations.text: In these five verses 'thought' is supposing something to be so: the disciples take Jesus for a ghost, the others take him for a spirit, the disciples take his word of sleep as rest, some take Judas's errand as a purchase, and Peter takes the angel's act for a vision. In each case the supposition is wrong. Verses: Mar 6:49, Luk 24:37, Joh 11:13, Joh 13:29, Act 12:9.
observations.grounds: they thought it was a ghost

observations.text: In 2Cor 9:5 and Phili 2:25 'thought it necessary' is judging or counting it needful: Paul decides on the sending he describes. Verses: 2Cor 9:5, Phili 2:25.
observations.grounds: I thought it necessary to urge

observations.text: In Act 26:8 'thought' is judged: Paul asks why it is judged incredible by the hearers that God raises the dead. Verses: Act 26:8.
observations.grounds: Why is it thought incredible by any

observations.text: In Luk 12:17 the Greek is the verb of saying; the English 'he thought to himself' renders it as what the man said in himself. It is inner speech. Verses: Luk 12:17.
observations.grounds: he thought to himself

observations.text: In 1Ti 3:7 'well thought of' is the Greek noun for testimony or good report: the overseer is to have a good report from those outside. It is how others speak of him, not what he thinks. Verses: 1Ti 3:7.
observations.grounds: well thought of by outsiders

observations.text: In 2Cor 10:5 'thought' is the mind's product: Paul takes every thought captive to obey Christ, set beside arguments and lofty opinions raised against the knowledge of God. Verses: 2Cor 10:5.
observations.grounds: take every thought captive to obey

observations.text: In Mat 20:10 and Act 8:20 'thought' is an assumption of the person: the workers hired first expect more, and Simon assumes the gift of God can be bought. In both the verse shows the assumption to be wrong. Verses: Mat 20:10, Act 8:20.
observations.grounds: they thought they would receive more

observations.text: In 1Cor 13:11 'thought' is how the child was minded; the verse sets it with speaking and reasoning as childish ways given up in adulthood. Verses: 1Cor 13:11.
observations.grounds: I thought like a child

observations.text: In Jon 1:6 this code is the Hebrew particle 'perhaps' in the captain's hope that the god may give a thought to them; it carries a possibility, with no thinking of its own. Verses: Jon 1:6.
observations.grounds: Perhaps the god will give a thought

observations.text: In these twenty-five verses 'thought' is the Hebrew verb of saying, quoting what a person says in himself: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, the servants, Saul, David's woman of Tekoa, Naaman, Hezekiah, the psalmist and others each state in a quoted sentence what they judged or expected, and the verse usually shows the thought wrong or about to be tested. It is inner speech about what will happen or what others mean. observations.text: In Pro 14:15 and Pro 21:29 'gives thought to his steps' is attending carefully to one's way: the prudent and the upright consider where they go, set against the simple and the wicked. Verses: Pro 14:15, Pro 21:29.
observations.grounds: the prudent gives thought to his steps

observations.text: In Deu 15:9 'thought' is the Hebrew word for a matter or word that arises in the heart, here an unworthy one against lending near the year of release. Verses: Deu 15:9.
observations.grounds: an unworthy thought in your heart

observations.text: In Num 33:56 'thought to do' is the Lord's own intention toward the Israelites if they fail to drive the people out: what he planned for others, he will do to them. Verses: Num 33:56.
observations.grounds: I thought to do to them

observations.text: In Psa 48:9 'thought on' is meditating on the Lord's steadfast love in the temple; the Hebrew is to dwell on something with the mind. Verses: Psa 48:9.
observations.grounds: We have thought on your steadfast love

observations.text: In Psa 50:21 'thought' is the false likeness the wicked imagine: that God is one like themselves. The Hebrew is of likening, and it is rebuked. Verses: Psa 50:21.
observations.grounds: you thought that I was one like

observations.text: In Deu 15:9 this code is the Hebrew verb 'to be' in the clause 'lest there be an unworthy thought'; it carries no thinking, which the noun of H1697 carries. Verses: Deu 15:9.
observations.grounds: Take care lest there be an unworthy

observations.text: In Lam 1:9 'took no thought' is the Hebrew verb of remembering: Jerusalem did not remember or consider her end. Verses: Lam 1:9.
observations.grounds: took no thought of her future

observations.text: In 1Sa 18:25 and Psa 40:17 'thought' is the Hebrew verb of devising and taking thought: Saul plans an end for David, and the Lord takes thought for the poor psalmist. In the first it is a plan against a person; in the second care for one. Verses: 1Sa 18:25, Psa 40:17.
